editorial:
You follow Romy, a powerful CEO who seems to have everything, until a young intern named Samuel pulls her into a risky affair. The story mixes office power, family pressure, and desire, so the mood feels tense and grown-up rather than sweet. Nicole Kidman and Harris Dickinson make the central push-and-pull feel sharp, and the film keeps you guessing about who is really in control. At home, her husband and daughters add real stakes, so every choice feels costly.

The acting is strong, the pacing stays tight, and the camera work makes every scene feel charged. Some viewers may find the power games uncomfortable or the ending a bit sudden, but the film is bold and hard to look away from. The chemistry keeps the tension high from start to finish. It is best for adults who like dark romance and workplace thrillers.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Romy finally refuses Samuel's control, ends the affair, and tells Jacob the truth. Jacob is hurt and angry, but they slowly reconnect instead of breaking apart. Samuel leaves the company, and Romy returns to her family with more control over her life. The last moments show her back in charge at work and home, though the marriage has clearly changed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark romance and workplace thrillers.
